pr_title: Fixed an issue where PluginsInitializer could not exit the loading screen
pr_body:
Fixed a bug that prevented PluginsInitializer from re-rendering to exit the loading screen when a plugin was not in the ready state.

Fix #21811

issue_context.body:
<!--

Before you start, please make sure your issue is understandable and reproducible.

https://guides.github.com/features/mastering-markdown/

Please ensure you have also read and understand the contributing guide.

## Bug report

### Required System information

<!-- Please ensure you are using the Node LTS version (18, 20, or 22) -->
<!-- Strapi v3 is no longer supported, please update to Strapi v4 -->
<!-- If you are reporting a frontend bug please provide error logs after setting STRAPI_ENFORCE_SOURCEMAPS=true in your .env -->
<!-- This environment variable makes frontend errors easier to read and trace -->

- Node.js version: v20.11.0
- NPM version: 10.2.4
- Strapi version: 5.0.6
- Database: SQLite
- Operating system: Windows
- Is your project Javascript or Typescript: Typescript

<!-- Did you know you can run `yarn strapi report` or `npm run strapi report` to get this information easier? -->

### Describe the bug
The following bug only happens in production mode when the project is deployed to azure. I was unable to reproduce it locally.
If you press F5 to get the entire site reloaded, sometimes you end up with an infinite loading (the blue loading spinner never ends).
There're no errors in the console.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Go to the admin page url in Chrome in incognito mode
2. If it loads, press F5 a few times. Sometimes the page loads, sometimes it doesn't and you'll end up with infinite loading.
3. If it doesn't load, press the Back button on the browser bar to get rid of the infinite loading. You can see the error either on the login screen or after getting logged in on the Home screen, or even in Content Manager.
4. See attached screenshot.

### Expected behavior

No infinite loading.

### Screenshots
![F5_timeout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b7f85db-bc7a-4835-a568-37cdf28205aa)

## package.json
"dependencies": {
    "@_sh/strapi-plugin-ckeditor": "^4.0.6",
    "@strapi/email": "5.0.6",
    "@strapi/plugin-cloud": "5.0.6",
    "@strapi/plugin-users-permissions": "5.0.6",
    "@strapi/strapi": "5.0.6",
    "better-sqlite3": "9.4.3",
    "moment": "^2.30.1",
    "mysql2": "^3.11.3",
    "react": "^18.0.0",
    "react-dom": "^18.0.0",
    "react-router-dom": "^6.0.0",
    "styled-components": "^6.0.0"
  }
  
  ## config
  All default in middlewares.ts except "frame-src" in "strapi::security" for strapi-plugin-ckeditor.

I spent several days to debug this issue and finally find out the cause and a possible workaround. However, I don't know how to fix it properly. Need help from Strapi dev team. cc @Convly 

TL; DR The `<PluginsInitializer>` becomes `memo` at runtime for unknown reason. The workaround is to make all plugins' `isReady: true` when calling `app.registerPlugin()` in plugin's `admin/src/index.js|ts`.

`<PluginsInitializer>` is designed to run all initializers of plugins. It will render `<Page.Loading />` if some plugins are not ready (the `isReady` flag), and it will render Admin Panel after all plugins are ready. The issue here is that `<PluginsInitializer>` becomes a memo component for unknown reason at runtime (verified by React Dev Tool) so that it will not re-render itself after all plugins are ready.

I don't know why `<PluginsInitializer>` becomes memo. `<PluginsInitializer>` has only one child which is a memo component (the `<DndProvider>`). Maybe React runtime does some magic in this scenario?

> The `<PluginsInitializer>` becomes memo at runtime for unknown reason.

I need to correct myself. It's not true. I just read a wrong value. The component type is `$$typeof: Symbol(react.element)`. However, `<PluginsInitializer>` did work like a memo component for unknown reason. The component render function returned correct value, but React didn't refresh component tree.

We also had trouble with Strapi stuck in loading state after authentication in production mode after upgrading to Strapi 5.8.x from Strapi 4 latest. We also were able to replicate it locally using `npm run build && npm run start` with both `NODE_ENV=production` and `NODE_ENV=local`. From what I can gather from the source code, there is a lifecycle issue in which Strapi admin does not finish waiting for the plugin to be `isReady` truthy, so it never triggers out of this block: https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/a4df7ad5ff6a4366442059f7c067a0424ba1e2f9/packages/core/admin/admin/src/components/PluginsInitializer.tsx#L49 I see that PR above is available, but we will wait for a stable version. Our temporary solution is to remove all offending plugins. Debugging steps for finding the plugin that's breaking for you: - Open inspector while stuck in loading state - Go to sources - Open `AuthenticatedLayout__.js` - Look for `isReady`, place debugger on that line - Find which plugin is initialized on `isReady: false` (screenshot) We were able to work around this plugin for now. If your offending plugin is a custom plugin, then the original solution of `isReady: true` on the `registerPlugin` should work. Otherwise, try removing the plugin if possible. We also originally tried patching the package itself as suggested above, but this was the cleanest solution for us. Patching the package also doesn't guarantee that it moved out of that returns block.

I cannot say for sure if it is really due to "produce" since others in the ticket have used my code without removing "produce". Therefore, I assume it has something to do with either lodash or the missing return in the case. Maybe just a `return draftState;` in the case would work as well. The case is definitely always being called, but React does not recognize that the object has changed and does not initiate a rerender.

According to the docs of `immer`, there is no need to return anything. `produce` should return a new object when it detects modification. But not needing `immer` and `lodash` for this simple operation is perhaps a good change in its own right.

I have found the cause of this problem: the `Plugin` class is not `immerable`. `immer` requires custom classes to be processed using `immerable`, otherwise changes on those classes are not detected by `produce()`.

See https://immerjs.github.io/immer/complex-objects
